document.title: Terrorism: Activities of Bin Ladin's in Pakistan, Afghanistan, and India
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: CIA Intelligence Report on bin Ladin's activities in Pakistan, Afghanistan and India. The Islamic Army treated Pakistan/Afghanistan as one region, a base and training center supporting insurgencies in Tajikistan, Kashmir and Chechnya, with a camp in Pakistan recruiting mostly Pakistanis. Source: 9/11 Commission Report, Chapter 2, Endnote 67.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Leader of the 'Islamic Army' who interviewed recruits and assigned them; based in Sudan at the time discussed

organizations.name: Islamic Army

sources_cited: CIA information report, not finally evaluated intelligence (14 July 1997)
key_claims: Pakistan and Afghanistan served as a regional base and training center for Islamic Army activities supporting insurgencies in Tajikistan, Kashmir and Chechnya.
The Islamic Army ran a camp in Pakistan to train and recruit members.
Bin Ladin personally interviewed recruits after training and selected their assignments.
Bin Ladin, based in Sudan, sourced fighting units from camps in Pakistan or elsewhere when he needed expertise.
